chunks: Sa'd narrated from Abū Ja'far, from al-'Abbās ibn Ma'rūf, from 'Alī ibn Mahziyār, from al-Ḥusayn ibn 'Alī, from someone he mentioned, from one of the two (Imams) عليهما السلام, that he said:
There is no harm in a man reciting in salat (prayer) while his garment is over his mouth.

So the proper way regarding these two reports is that we understand them to mean that if the face-covering does not prevent the Qur'an from being heard, then there is no harm in it. It is only considered disliked when it prevents the recitation from being heard. This is indicated by that.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual prayer in which recitation takes place
key_terms.اللِّثَامُ: face-covering or veil over the mouth
key_terms.الْقُرْآنِ: the Qur'an, whose recitation must remain hearable
key_terms.الْقِرَاءَةِ: recitation, specifically the audible recitation in prayer
key_terms.ثَوْبُهُ: his garment, used here as a covering over the mouth
key_terms.فِيهِ: his mouth, the place being covered during recitation
key_terms.كُرِهَ: it is disliked, indicating reprehensibility rather than prohibition
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm, indicating permissibility

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to recite in salat (prayer) while covering the mouth with a garment or face-covering?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling on reciting in salat (prayer) while covering the mouth with a garment or face-covering. It indicates permissibility when the covering does not obstruct the hearing of the Qur'anic recitation, while disapproval applies when it hinders the recitation from being heard.
